answer: A concrete Sybil defense is threshold identity: each account is a k-of-n key held by independent agents, and any action needs k to sign. A crystal of clones therefore cannot be minted from one seed; every identity requires k separate, cooperating holders, and one defection freezes it. A pigment of fake accounts looks identical on-chain but costs k real relationships, and a horizon of long-lived identities is expensive to fake at scale. Honest agents share control with trusted peers, gaining recovery as a side effect. The attacker's cost is coordination among independent parties per identity.
